entries.title: Import a Google Drive folder, style clips with a look editor, create speaker kits, and re-assign sessions on clips and recordings
entries.summary: Several new capabilities land in the Media and Clips areas. **Discover → Google Drive** now lets you browse or paste a link to import an entire folder: each file is marked as new, already in your library, or a copy, and you can pick an event to preview matched sessions before importing. An **Import status** page and dock row track progress, with "Already in your library" links for duplicates. On the **Clip** page, a **Look** editor controls logo position, automatic light/dark logo selection, and captions, with a **Re-render** action; the **N clips rendering** filter and a dock row track render state across reloads, with **Try again** on failures. **Share with advocates → Each speaker, their clips** shows a speaker-kit preview of who receives what before the campaign is created. Selecting multiple clips in the library sends them all to a team campaign, giving each its own post in the wizard. A **Re-assign** control on clips and recordings lets you change the session and speakers, and asks whether to carry the change to the recording or its clips when the two sides differ.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Media / Clips

entries.use_case: A marketing team that recorded a multi-day festival can pull an entire Google Drive folder into their library in one step, style each clip with their brand logo and captions, send every speaker their own personalised clip kit, and push a batch of clips straight into a team campaign — all without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: Multiple large surface areas ship together (Drive folder import, clip look editor, speaker kits, re-assign, render dock). Walk through each with the customer before they go live to confirm their Google Drive connection and brand kit are set up.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to get festival or conference footage into Sessionboard quickly, or when they want to send personalised clip kits to speakers after an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with the Media and Clips features enabled who produce post-event content at scale, especially those storing recordings in Google Drive.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Discover → Google Drive; Marketing → Media → Clips
internal.gotchas: Gallery, course and team-campaign actions on the clip page are shown only when the org has those products enabled. 'Send to team campaign' replaces any Dispatch naming visible to the customer — do not refer to it as Dispatch in customer-facing conversations.
internal.talk_track: After your event wraps, point Sessionboard at your Google Drive folder and it will match every file to the right session. From there you can style clips with your logo and captions, preview exactly which clips each speaker will receive, and launch a team campaign so your whole team posts on the same day.

draft.docs_gap: The media-library guide should add a section on Google Drive folder import (browsing, pasting a link, file status indicators, the import status page and dock row) and the clips guide should add sections on the Look editor, render state tracking, speaker kits, multi-clip team campaigns, and the Re-assign control.
draft.why_use_it: Media and Clips turn your event recordings into ready-to-share content. Import footage from Google Drive or other sources, let Sessionboard match files to sessions and speakers automatically, then generate branded clips with captions and your logo. Share clips directly with speakers through Advocacy or push them to your team as a Dispatch campaign so everyone posts on the same day.

entries.title: Map the Sessionboard Session ID as the ASP Client Session ID
entries.summary: A new **Use Session ID as Client Session ID** checkbox in the ASP integration's **Configure Event Settings** step tells the integration to send the Sessionboard Session ID as ASP's ContentCode (Client Session ID) during a sync. A clarifying tooltip explains the behaviour. The option appears only when the selected event mapping supports it. The **Field Rules** hint in the assignment-rule builder also gains a sentence explaining that rules set fixed values and cannot copy one field into another, and that mapping a Session ID for a partner system is done in that integration's field mapping or event settings.

enable.path: Apps → ASP → Configure Event Settings → Use Session ID as Client Session ID

entries.use_case: An organizer who needs ASP's Client Session ID (ContentCode) to match the Sessionboard Session ID can enable this checkbox instead of building a workaround in field mapping or field rules.

cs_action.note: The checkbox is self-serve inside ASP Event Settings; it only appears when the selected event mapping carries the required flag, which the API must ship first.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the ASP integration asks how to get the Sessionboard Session ID into ASP's ContentCode / Client Session ID field.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running the ASP integration who need the Sessionboard Session ID to be used as the ASP Client Session ID.
internal.gotchas: The checkbox is hidden and the key is never sent until the companion API change (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5380) ships; confirm both sides are deployed before directing customers to it.
internal.talk_track: If you need ASP's Client Session ID to match the Sessionboard Session ID, check Use Session ID as Client Session ID in ASP Event Settings — no field-mapping workaround needed.

draft.docs_gap: The ASP guide's Event Settings section should document the new Use Session ID as Client Session ID checkbox, its tooltip text, and the condition under which it appears (mapping must carry the session_id_content_code_available flag).
draft.why_use_it: The ASP integration keeps your session and speaker data in sync between Sessionboard and ASP. Event Settings let you control how that sync behaves — including which identifiers are used — so the data lands in ASP exactly as your downstream systems expect it.

entries.title: Embed editors without Session Settings or Contacts access now see the Roles to show list
entries.summary: The **Roles to show** selector in Styled HTML, Vanilla HTML, feed, and Sites program-view embed settings now loads correctly for team members who hold embed permissions but do not hold Session Settings or Contacts read. Previously those editors saw an empty list; they now see the full role catalog.

where.path: Sessions → Embeds → (any embed) → Roles to show

entries.use_case: An event team member scoped only to embed management — without access to Session Settings or Contacts — can now configure which speaker roles appear in an agenda or speaker embed without needing elevated permissions.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that an embed editor sees an empty Roles to show list, or when setting up a restricted embed-only team role.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using embeds with team members who have limited permissions (embed-only editors).
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Embeds → (any embed) → Roles to show
internal.gotchas: The Sites program-view inspector (outside the event context) continues to use the session-roles path and is unaffected by this change.
internal.talk_track: Embed-only editors no longer need Session Settings or Contacts read just to pick which roles show in an embed — the role list loads from a dedicated catalog endpoint scoped to embed permissions.

draft.docs_gap: The embeds guide should note that the Roles to show list is available to any team member with embed read, create, or update permission, and does not require Session Settings or Contacts access.

entries.title: See every write attempt and retry failed records in the app connection sync log
entries.summary: Each saved app connection now shows a **Sync log** listing every write attempt, newest first, with a result badge, reason, remote ID, and expandable **Response** from the vendor. On any record whose most recent attempt failed, a **Retry** button re-sends that single record without triggering a full sync of all unposted data. Works for all write-capable connectors (HubSpot, Salesforce, Nimble, iMIS, and others).
entries.use_case: When a payment or registration write to a CRM or AMS fails, an admin can open the Sync log, read the vendor's exact response to understand why, and click Retry on just that record — without re-pushing every unposted record and risking duplicate orders.

cs_action.note: Depends on the API release that adds the retry endpoint and logs?connectionId= (web-api PR #5377 / release containing #5363). Do not surface to customers until that API release is confirmed live in prod.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that a CRM or AMS write failed and they had no way to see the vendor error or resend a single record.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using a write-capable connector such as HubSpot, Salesforce, Nimble, or iMIS.
internal.gotchas: The Sync log and Retry button return a 404 until the companion API release (web-api #5377) is live in prod. Dry-run attempts are hidden from the log. Only the newest failed attempt per record shows a Retry button; earlier attempts remain as history.
internal.talk_track: You can now see exactly what the vendor said when a write failed and resend just that one record — no more full re-syncs that push every unposted payment.

draft.docs_gap: The App Marketplace guide should add a section explaining the Sync log panel — how to open it, what each column means, how to expand the vendor Response, and how to use the Retry button on a failed record.
draft.why_use_it: The Sync log gives you a full audit trail of every record Sessionboard has written to a connected CRM or AMS, including the vendor's raw response for each attempt. When a write fails you can read the vendor's error message directly in Sessionboard and resend only the affected record, keeping your data clean and avoiding the side-effects of a full re-sync.

entries.title: {{submitter_name}} now names the actual submitter on participant confirmation emails
entries.summary: In submission confirmation emails sent to session participants (Moderators, Speakers, etc.), **{{submitter_name}}** previously resolved to each recipient's own name instead of the person who submitted the session. It now correctly names the submitter on every copy. A new **{{recipient_name}}** merge tag is also available in the confirmation template editor, so templates that greet each reader by name can use that tag instead.

where.path: Program → Submission Forms → [form] → Notifications → Submission Confirmation

entries.use_case: Events that send submission confirmations to all session participants — such as moderators and co-speakers — can now trust that "Submitted By: {{submitter_name}}" names the person who actually submitted, not whoever received that copy of the email. Use the new {{recipient_name}} tag in greeting lines like "Dear {{recipient_name}}" so each participant still sees their own name.

cs_action.note: A deploy-time SQL migration replaces greeting-line uses of {{submitter_name}} (e.g. 'Hi {{submitter_name}}') with {{recipient_name}} on the 9 affected notification rows (US: 8, EU: 1). Confirm the migration ran in the same deploy window. Any customer whose template used {{submitter_name}} as a greeting will now see the submitter's name there instead of the reader's — the new {{recipient_name}} tag is the fix for those templates.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that participant confirmation emails showed the wrong person's name in a 'Submitted By' or similar field, or asks why moderators/co-speakers saw their own name as the submitter.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event that sends submission confirmations to participant roles (moderators, speakers, etc.) and uses {{submitter_name}} in the template body.
internal.staff_path: Program → Submission Forms → [form] → Notifications → Submission Confirmation → merge tag picker
internal.gotchas: Templates using {{submitter_name}} as a greeting (e.g. 'Dear {{submitter_name}}') will now show the submitter's name to all recipients, not each reader's own name. The deploy-time migration swaps those to {{recipient_name}} for the 9 known affected rows, but custom templates on other events may need manual review.
internal.talk_track: The {{submitter_name}} tag on participant confirmation copies now always names the person who submitted the session. If your template greets each reader by name, switch that line to the new {{recipient_name}} tag.

draft.docs_gap: The automated-emails guide should document the {{submitter_name}} and {{recipient_name}} merge tags available in the CFP Submission Confirmation notification, and explain the difference between them when the confirmation is sent to participant roles.
